Musk Hints at More Tesla Lineup Culling, Model Y Will Only Be a Seven-Seater With No Steering Wheel
10 photos
Photo: Tesla
After sounding the death knell for the Model S, Model X, and then the Cybertruck, Elon Musk now wants Tesla to trim the Model Y lineup. In a recent interview, he said that demand for the long-wheelbase variant Model Y L is so strong that Tesla could drop all other trims. This will eventually be the only Model Y available, and it won't have a steering wheel and pedals, just like the Cybercab.
Tesla is holding a shareholder meeting on December 3, and it's all about giving Elon Musk more power. Officially, the agenda includes the re-election of Musk, Robyn Denholm, and JB Straubel to the Board of Directors and the approval of the 2025 executive compensation package, including about $158.4 billion in 2025 stock awards to Musk.
Unofficially, the meeting will give more power to Musk and the board by debuting the automatic voting, or Tesla's Voluntary Retail Voting Program. This essentially locks investor votes with the board for future votes if they agree to participate. It is also expected that Musk will officially announce a future merger with SpaceX .
More importantly, Musk will use the meeting to double down on his plans for Tesla to phase out vehicle manufacturing. He said a while back that the Roadster would be the last driver's car from Tesla, and he appears to do whatever he can to keep his promise. That is, if Tesla shareholders don't stop this madness.
Musk has started by culling Tesla's lineup, first by killing the Model S and Model X earlier this year. The Cybertruck followed shortly, with the stainless steel truck slated for an untimely demise next summer. Although it was obvious that the Model 3 might follow next, it appears that not even the Model Y is safe from the axe.
Photo: Tesla During a recent interview at the New York Times DealBook Summit, Musk said that the demand for the long-wheelbase Model Y L is off the charts. That's the good part. The bad part is that Musk has gotten the idea that Tesla should stop building all other variants of the Model Y and focus its entire production on the Model Y L.
If that wasn't controversial enough, Musk went on to say that people won't be able to drive this Model Y variant in the near future. Instead, Musk said that Tesla would build an autonomous version of the Model Y that won't have a steering wheel or pedals. That's the same Model Y L, though, because he also said that this autonomous variant should be able to transport groups of six or seven people.
So, there you have it, folks, another installment of the same "Tesla is not a carmaker" franchise. I'm not sure what timeline Musk set for these changes. From where I stand, it appears that he is already planning for a world without human drivers, even if autonomous vehicles are only allowed in some small areas in a few cities in the world. Wiping out the entire Tesla's vehicle lineup to build more parking lot decorations seems like a sure way of ensuring that Tesla doesn't survive .
As for when the Model 3 will disappear, it suffices to say that the sedan doesn't address any untapped transportation needs. The Cybercab is cheap to build and convenient to operate, while the Model Y has the advantage of accommodating more passengers, but the Model 3? It has a target on its back already. Elon says @Tesla will introduce a fully autonomous version of the Model Y with no steering wheel or pedals: "It's going to make sense for us to make cars that can seat different amounts of people. We still need autonomous vehicles if you've got 4 or 6, or a whole family. What we plan to do is have an autonomous version of the Model Y that won't have steering wheels or pedals and would be good for transporting groups of 6 or 7 people." (via NYT Dealbook Summit today) — Sawyer Merritt (@SawyerMerritt) November 18, 2026
